answer_text:
Yes, the limit is always \(0\) for every continuous \(f\in C[0,1]\).

We prove this explicitly.

For \(n\ge 1\), we first compute \(T^n\). A direct induction shows that for \(x>0\),

\[
(T^n f)(x)=\frac{1}{(n-1)!x}\int_0^x \left(\log\frac{x}{t}\right)^{n-1} f(t)\,dt.
\]

Indeed, for \(n=1\) this is exactly the definition of \(T\). If it holds for \(n\), then

\[
\begin{aligned}
(T^{n+1}f)(x)
&=\frac1x\int_0^x (T^n f)(s)\,ds \\
&=\frac{1}{x(n-1)!}\int_0^x\int_0^s \frac{1}{s}
\left(\log\frac{s}{t}\right)^{n-1} f(t)\,dt\,ds.
\end{aligned}
\]

Interchanging the order of integration and evaluating the inner integral gives

\[
\int_t^x \frac{1}{s}\left(\log\frac{s}{t}\right)^{n-1}\,ds
=\frac{1}{n}\left(\log\frac{x}{t}\right)^n,
\]

so

\[
(T^{n+1}f)(x)=\frac{1}{n!x}\int_0^x
\left(\log\frac{x}{t}\right)^n f(t)\,dt.
\]

Now let

\[
g=f-f(0)\cdot 1.
\]

Then \(g(0)=0\), and since \(T\) leaves constants fixed,

\[
T^n(f)-f(0)=T^n(g).
\]

For \(x\in(0,1]\), using the formula above,

\[
(T^n g)(x)=\frac{1}{(n-1)!x}\int_0^x
\left(\log\frac{x}{t}\right)^{n-1}g(t)\,dt.
\]

Make the substitution \(t=xe^{-u}\). Then \(dt=-xe^{-u}\,du\), and

\[
(T^n g)(x)=\frac{1}{(n-1)!}\int_0^\infty
u^{n-1}e^{-u} g(xe^{-u})\,du.
\]

The measure

\[
d\mu_n(u)=\frac{u^{n-1}e^{-u}}{(n-1)!}\,du
\]

is a probability measure on \((0,\infty)\). Thus

\[
|(T^n g)(x)|
\le \int_0^\infty |g(xe^{-u})|\,d\mu_n(u).
\]

Fix \(\varepsilon>0\). Since \(g\) is continuous at \(0\) and \(g(0)=0\), there exists \(\delta\in(0,1)\) such that

\[
|g(t)|<\varepsilon \qquad \text{whenever }0\le t\le \delta.
\]

Let

\[
a=-\log \delta>0.
\]

Then for \(u\ge a\),

\[
xe^{-u}\le e^{-u}\le e^{-a}=\delta,
\]

so \(|g(xe^{-u})|<\varepsilon\). Therefore, for every \(x\in(0,1]\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
|(T^n g)(x)|
&\le \int_0^a |g(xe^{-u})|\,d\mu_n(u)
+\int_a^\infty |g(xe^{-u})|\,d\mu_n(u) \\
&\le 2\|f\|_\infty\,\mu_n([0,a))+\varepsilon.
\end{aligned}
\]

But

\[
\mu_n([0,a))
=\int_0^a \frac{u^{n-1}e^{-u}}{(n-1)!}\,du
\le \int_0^a \frac{u^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\,du
=\frac{a^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\to 0
\qquad (n\to\infty).
\]

Hence

\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\|T^n(f)-f(0)\|_\infty
\le \varepsilon.
\]

Since \(\varepsilon>0\) was arbitrary,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\|T^n(f)-f(0)\|_\infty=0.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
